summary: The shot is a locked, static torso with one arm gesture that pops in fast, leaves the frame, and repeats identically 3.5 s later. The wagging finger the idea calls for never reads.

faults.what: The arm swings up from rest into frame in about 4 frames (29.99 to 30.09), with no anticipation and no body lead. The torso and shoulders stay frozen while the forearm whips in, so the arm looks driven on its own.
faults.fix: Add a small shoulder and torso lean or drop before the lift. Ease the arm in over about 8 to 10 frames and let it settle.

faults.what: The gesturing hand is cut off by the left frame edge from 30.13 to 30.23. The hand, which is the point of the shot, is mostly out of frame.
faults.fix: Reframe wider or shift the camera left. Alternatively, pull the gesture in so the hand stays inside the frame.

faults.what: The idea is a wagging finger that drives the point home. The hand reads as a loose fist or open claw at the frame edge, and no finger point or wag is visible.
faults.fix: Pose the hand with the index finger extended. Bring it inside the frame and add a clear side-to-side wag.

faults.what: Frames 33.49 to 33.73 repeat 29.99 to 30.23 exactly: same arm path, same head tilt, same framing. The gesture is a copied loop, so it reads as canned rather than emphatic. It lands as a repeat instead of building a point.
faults.fix: Vary the second gesture with a different amplitude, timing or hand. Alternatively, hold a stronger pose and cut the repeat.

faults.what: Before the gesture (29.46 to 29.70), the body drifts slightly with a stiff, near-symmetrical stance and the arms hanging. There is no clear held pose and little face change, so the character looks idle and blank rather than meaning it.
faults.fix: Hold a stronger pose with a head or eye shift and a blink. Start the gesture earlier.
